analysis: The only change in this file is at line 313 of EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift: the test helper recordServerStream now ignores a new `.logprobs` case in the MLXServerGenerationEvent switch (`case .toolCall, .toolCallDelta, .logprobs: continue`). This is test-only code, so no production control, key custody, attestation, authorization, or encryption behavior changes. It uses stub engines, a fabricated ModelContainer and isolated runtimes, with no network and no real weights. I read the rest of the file, which is unchanged context: the KV re-slicing, fair-share, restore-on-throw, reslice-floor and gate-race tests. None of it touches the T-041 prefix-cache at-rest surface (SSD tier, HMAC names, TTL, salt scoping), and no production gate, TTL or lookup-key derivation is modified. The new `.logprobs` event is discarded by this helper, which may mean the test no longer asserts on logprob output in that stream. That is a minor test-coverage point, not a security regression. Whether the production code that emits `.logprobs` (a source change in another unit or batch) handles logprobs safely is outside the supplied evidence. Integration should check that logprob data does not leak beyond the E2E-encrypted response path (T-008, A-001). Nothing in this file supports a finding.
